children: is expected to show an improvement in its losses compared to a year ago when it reports its third-quarter earnings on November 9 after the closing bell. Analysts are also expected to closely follow management’s commentary on its cash flow improvement and updates on the firm’s liquidity.
Wall Street has priced in a 16.6% improvement in its bottom line at
per share, while revenue is projected to improve 18.6% to $399.14M. Over the last 3 months, EPS estimates have seen no
but 4 downward moves. Revenue estimates have seen 1 upward revision and 6 downward moves—representing a bearish inclination among analysts.

“Lucid's profitability profile, however, will nevertheless remain pressured in the quarters ahead as the electric vehicle company suffers from sluggish demand for its high-priced EVs in the luxury segment,” Seeking Alpha analyst
Highly negative gross margins (97% on a trailing-twelve-months basis) as well as negative free cash flow (cash burn) are also challenges the company needs to overcome, the analyst added.
Last quarter, management said it will provide details on the progress of its $1.4B cash flow improvement for 2026, during the Q3 print.
“We will also provide a progress update on the Nuro, Uber Robotaxi project, and on the latest advancements of our AMP-2 factory readiness,” CEO Silvio Napoli said.

Earlier in October, the EV-maker reported a 6.7% drop in its Q3 deliveries—in line with the management’s earlier guidance—following the reduction of its U.S. workforce by one-fifth and elimination of the second shift at its Arizona facility.
The New Jersey-based firm delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, beating expectations for 3,709 deliveries, but produced only 2,954.
Going into the earnings, investors are expected to scrutinize the firm’s revised execution strategy, especially under its new Chief Financial Officer, Alexander De Bock, who took charge in July.
Over the last 2 years, LCID has beaten EPS estimates 50% of the time and has beaten revenue estimates 38% of the time.

The stock has declined more than 69% in the year so far, while in the past year, it has plunged 83%. It has been rated as a Strong Sell per Seeking Alpha’s quant rating, while analysts have issued a Hold call.
